description: Compute a diversity / origination / extinction curve for a clade across geologic time, binned by period, epoch, or age — answers "plot dinosaur genus diversity across the Mesozoic." Pass a clade-inclusive base_name (or base_id, the same clade by resolved taxon id — exactly one of the two) and bound the span by a named interval (e.g. "Mesozoic") or a max_ma/min_ma range; choose what to count (genera, species, or families) and the bin resolution. The full bin set returns inline — a diversity series is a bounded set of geologic intervals — so you read the curve, the turnover, and the per-bin origination/extinction directly. Counts reflect SAMPLED diversity, biased by collection effort and rock availability, not true past diversity.

base_id.description: Clade-inclusive taxon to count, by PBDB taxon id — the taxon_no from paleobiology_get_taxon, or accepted_no on an occurrence row. Same semantics as base_name, but unambiguous where a name is not (homonyms, synonyms, unresolved spellings). Supply this or base_name (exactly one is required, never both).

base_name.description: Clade-inclusive taxon to count, e.g. "Dinosauria" or "Ammonoidea" — this taxon and all descendants. Supply this or base_id (exactly one is required, never both).

count.description: What to count per bin: "genera" (default), "species", or "families".

interval.description: Named geologic interval bounding the span, e.g. "Mesozoic". Alternative to max_ma/min_ma.

max_ma.description: Older bound of the span in millions of years ago. Alternative to interval. When paired with min_ma it must be strictly greater — max_ma is the deeper-time end of the span.

min_ma.description: Younger bound of the span in millions of years ago. Alternative to interval. When paired with max_ma it must be strictly smaller — min_ma is the nearer-to-present end of the span.

name: paleobiology_get_diversity

attribution.description: CC-BY data attribution for the Paleobiology Database.

bins.description: Per-interval diversity bins over the span, ordered oldest-first (oldest geologic interval, highest max_ma, first).

items.description: One diversity bin (a single geologic interval) with turnover counts.

extinctions.description: Taxa whose last appearance is in this bin (LADs, including bin-only singletons).

implied.description: Range-through taxa implied present in the bin but without an occurrence in it.

max_ma.description: Older boundary of the bin in millions of years ago.

min_ma.description: Younger boundary of the bin in millions of years ago.

n_occurrences.description: Total fossil occurrences counted in this bin.

originations.description: Taxa whose first appearance is in this bin (new FADs, including bin-only singletons).

range_through.description: Taxa whose range crosses both boundaries of this bin (present before and after).

sampled_in_bin.description: Taxa with at least one occurrence inside this bin.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `missing_filter`: Neither base_name nor base_id was supplied — a diversity curve needs a clade to count. `conflicting_taxon_filter`: Both base_name and base_id were supplied — PBDB accepts only one clade selector. `inverted_ma_range`: min_ma was greater than or equal to max_ma — the span is inverted or empty. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Guidance when the clade or span produced no bins, or when the taxon name could not be resolved and was ignored.

title: paleobiology-mcp-server: diversity through time
